rows.selection_reason: With no prior experiments, the most critical need is to establish a clean, well-defined baseline for the multimodal setting. config_007 (multimodal, singleprofile, pca_n2000, resnet50, weighted) uses the most standard and well-understood component at every design dimension: a simple linear RNA encoder (pca_n2000), a widely-used image backbone (resnet50), a single profile (avoiding confounding from multiprofile aggregation), and a simple weighted fusion. This gives a reference performance against which all future experiments can isolate the effect of changing one dimension (e.g., swapping to scgpt, adding multiprofile with avgpool, or trying concat fusion). Starting with this 'control' configuration maximizes the information gained per experiment, because every subsequent result can be interpreted as a delta from a known anchor, reducing uncertainty about which design choices matter.

With only one completed experiment (config_007: multimodal, singleprofile, pca_n2000, resnet50, weighted fusion → 52.3% acc), the most critical uncertainty is whether the multimodal fusion is actually adding value over the image modality alone. config_002 (image_only, singleprofile, resnet50) is the cleanest possible comparison: it holds the image encoder (resnet50) and profile setting (singleprofile) identical to config_007 while removing the RNA branch entirely. If image-only performance is close to or exceeds 52.3%, the current RNA encoding (pca_n2000) with weighted fusion is not contributing, and future effort should target better RNA representations or fusion strategies. If image-only is substantially lower, multimodal fusion is confirmed as beneficial and we can then efficiently explore fusion type, aggregation, and encoder upgrades. Resolving this fundamental question before varying fusion, aggregation, or encoders avoids wasting budget on secondary design choices while the primary 'does multimodal help?' question remains unanswered.

Evidence: config_007 (multimodal, singleprofile, pca_n2000, resnet50, weighted) achieved 0.5232 acc, while config_002 (image_only, singleprofile, resnet50) achieved only 0.2079 acc. This large gap shows the RNA modality is critical, but we cannot yet decompose whether RNA alone drives most of the signal or whether there is genuine multimodal synergy. Uncertainty: We lack an RNA-only baseline to attribute performance to each modality. This experiment (config_019: rna_only, singleprofile, pca_n2000) is a clean ablation of config_007 with the image removed, holding RNA encoder and profile setting constant. It will clarify: (a) if RNA alone ≈ 0.5, the image adds little and we should focus on RNA representation; (b) if RNA alone is much lower (~0.2-0.3), there is true multimodal synergy and fusion strategy becomes the key design axis. This is the best use of the next budget slot because it completes the fundamental modality decomposition (image_only / rna_only / multimodal) before investing in more complex configurations (multiprofile, different encoders, aggregation), ensuring subsequent experiments target the right design dimensions.

Evidence: config_007 (multimodal, pca_n2000, resnet50, weighted) achieves 0.5232 acc, while RNA-only pca_n2000 (config_019) achieves 0.4849 and image-only resnet50 (config_002) only 0.2079. RNA is clearly the dominant signal, and the multimodal gain over RNA-only is modest (+0.038). The only RNA encoder tested so far is pca_n2000, a simple linear projection. Uncertainty: whether a learned, generative RNA representation (scgpt) meaningfully improves the dominant modality's contribution. This experiment (config_034) changes exactly one factor from config_007—RNA encoder from pca_n2000 to scgpt—while holding image encoder (resnet50), profile (single), and fusion (weighted) constant. If scgpt substantially outperforms pca_n2000, it tells us to invest in richer RNA representations as the highest-leverage design choice; if not, it confirms pca_n2000 is near-sufficient and redirects budget toward multiprofile or image-encoder improvements. This is the most informative single-factor test under the limited budget because it isolates the effect on the modality that carries most of the signal.

Evidence: config_007 (pca_n2000, resnet50, weighted fusion, singleprofile, multimodal) is our best result at 0.523 acc, but it is only marginally better than rna_only (0.485), and we have only tested weighted fusion so far. The RNA encoder choice (pca_n2000 vs scgpt) showed a large effect, but fusion strategy remains entirely untested. Question: Does concat fusion outperform weighted fusion when all other variables are held constant? config_041 is identical to config_007 except fusion changes from weighted to concat, making it a clean single-variable comparison. Why best next experiment: Fusion is a fundamental design axis for every multimodal configuration; resolving it now prevents us from carrying a suboptimal fusion choice into all subsequent multiprofile or encoder-variation experiments. It is low-risk (worst case confirms weighted is fine) and high-information (a large gap would redirect the entire search), making it the most efficient use of the next budget slot under the principle of isolating one design variable.

Evidence: All five completed experiments are singleprofile. PCA_n2000 clearly outperforms scgpt as RNA encoder (0.523 vs 0.421), and concat fusion marginally beats weighted (0.527 vs 0.523) with pca_n2000+resnet50. RNA dominates over image (0.485 vs 0.208), and multimodal adds ~4 pts over RNA alone. The largest unexplored design axis is multiprofile aggregation—no multiprofile experiment has been run yet. Question: Does aggregating multiple profiles (via avgpool) on top of our best singleprofile settings (pca_n2000, resnet50, concat) improve validation accuracy, or does it dilute the signal? Why this experiment: config_008 is the minimal, direct extension of our best result (config_041) by adding only the multiprofile+avgpool aggregation step, isolating that single design choice. Avgpool is the simpler aggregation; if it fails to help, a more complex transformer aggregation is less likely to. This single experiment resolves whether the multiprofile axis is worth further investment under our limited budget.

The strongest evidence so far is that multiprofile with pca_n2000/resnet50/avgpool/concat (config_008, acc 0.619) dramatically outperforms all singleprofile configurations (~0.52–0.53), confirming that multiprofile is the key design lever. However, we have only tested one aggregation strategy (avgpool) in the multiprofile setting. Aggregation determines how multiple profiles are combined before fusion and is arguably the most impactful untested design choice in this regime—transformer aggregation could capture profile-to-profile interactions that a simple average misses. config_006 (multimodal, multiprofile, pca_n2000, resnet50, transformer, concat) changes only the aggregation from avgpool to transformer while holding every other factor identical to config_008, giving a clean single-variable comparison. This is the best use of the next budget slot because it isolates the highest-uncertainty, highest-impact design decision in our currently best-performing family, and the result will directly inform whether further investment in multiprofile transformer-based models is warranted.

The best-performing experiment so far is config_008 (multimodal, multiprofile, pca_n2000, resnet50, avgpool, concat; acc=0.619), which shows that multiprofile + avgpool aggregation + concat fusion is a strong design. However, the image modality's contribution remains uncertain: image_only with resnet50 was very weak (acc=0.208), and we have not yet tested whether a stronger image encoder (imagenet_vit_l) can unlock more signal from the image branch. config_043 is identical to config_008 except it swaps resnet50 for imagenet_vit_l, making it a clean single-variable comparison that isolates the image encoder effect in the best-performing setting. This is the highest-value next experiment because (1) it exploits the strongest known configuration, (2) it tests an unexplored and potentially impactful design axis (image encoder quality), (3) a positive result would open a clear exploitation path, while a null result would confirm that the image modality's ceiling is low regardless of encoder, redirecting effort toward RNA-side improvements.

Evidence: config_043 (multiprofile, pca_n2000, imagenet_vit_l, avgpool, concat) is the current best at 0.6287 acc. In singleprofile, concat and weighted fusion are nearly identical (0.5266 vs 0.5232), and in multiprofile with resnet50 we've only tested concat (config_008: 0.6186). We have no multiprofile+ViT data point for weighted fusion. Question: Does weighted fusion match or beat concat in the best-performing multiprofile+ViT+avgpool setup? This isolates the single variable of fusion strategy while holding all other choices at their empirically best values. Rationale: Under a limited budget, a one-variable extension of the top configuration is the most efficient way to either confirm concat's advantage (locking in the design) or discover that weighted fusion is equally good (freeing a design degree for future experiments). It avoids the risk of changing multiple variables (e.g., aggregation + fusion) and directly informs whether the current best can be improved or whether we should pivot to exploring other axes (RNA encoder, aggregation) next.

The current best configuration (config_042: multimodal, multiprofile, pca_n2000, imagenet_vit_l, avgpool, weighted; acc=0.6352) establishes that multi-profile + ViT-L + avgpool + weighted fusion is the strongest combination. However, the RNA encoder has only been tested as pca_n2000 in this setting, while scvi_n200 remains completely untested. In single-profile settings, scgpt underperformed pca_n2000 (0.4214 vs 0.5232), but scvi_n200 is a different learned representation that has not been evaluated. Config_047 changes only the RNA encoder from pca_n2000 to scvi_n200 while holding all other hyperparameters at their best-known values, cleanly isolating the effect of the RNA representation. This is the highest-value next experiment because it tests the single most important unexplored design axis in the current best region, and the result will determine whether further investment should go toward learned RNA encoders or toward other dimensions (aggregation, fusion) with PCA fixed.
